title: Signed total homotopies and naturality of the internal condensed bar
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent site of profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff and an inverse limit of finite discrete groups), with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Write $\mathcal M_A$ for internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and $\mathcal E_A$ for modules with $A$-linear $\underline G$-action and equivariant maps [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $U:\mathcal E_A\to\mathcal M_A$ forget the action and $\Gamma_G$ take the invariant submodule, fixed after every profinite base change. For a profinite parameter $S$, $A[S]$ is the free internal module on its representable condensed set; $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ is internal module Hom, right adjoint to tensor. Use the internal bar diagrams of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. For any nonnegative complex $I^\bullet$ in $\mathcal E_A$, write $D(I)^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],UI^q)$ with the action-dependent inhomogeneous differential and vertical differential induced by $I$. Use $\operatorname{Tot}D(I)$ with differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_I$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. An equivariant chain map $f:I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ induces a map $\operatorname{Tot}D(f)$ commuting with the invariant augmentations $b_I,b_J$. If $f-g=d_Jh+hd_I$ for an equivariant chain homotopy $h^q:I^q\to J^{q-1}$, then
$$H|_{D(I)^{p,q}}=(-1)^p\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],Uh^q)$$
is a total homotopy: $\operatorname{Tot}D(f)-\operatorname{Tot}D(g)=dH+Hd$. It is compatible with the homotopy obtained by applying $\Gamma_G$ on the augmentation source.
For nonnegative equivariant injective resolutions of modules $N,M$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], every map $N\to M$ admits such a chain lift, and any two lifts induce the same map after localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Between two resolutions of $N$, lifts of the identity induce mutually inverse derived isomorphisms of bar totals. They satisfy identity and composition compatibility. Suppose $U$ is exact and preserves injectives. Under the canonical derived-unit comparisons on these resolutions [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], the column maps are precisely the derived internal-Hom maps, the invariant-source maps are precisely $R\Gamma_G$ of the module map, and the localized augmentation square commutes. Consequently the augmentation comparison on specified resolutions is independent of resolutions and natural in the equivariant module.

proof.text: Package the additive functors N ↦ C^p(N) and the bar differentials as a nonnegative complex in the category of additive functors. Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorMapHomotopy₂ to evaluation and the coefficient homotopy, with identity on this fixed complex. Its explicit summand formula has coefficient ε₂(p,q−1)=(-1)^p. The bicomplex and induced total map agree with doubleComplex and totalCochains by their definitions. If the target diagonal is absent, ιTotalOrZero is zero; the homotopy zero condition handles the q=0 boundary. This yields the stated formula with q−1 replaced by m−p. At bar degree zero, TotalAugmentation.components and Augmentation.map.naturality identify its restriction with the invariant homotopy.

proof.text: Mathlib InjectiveResolution.desc and desc_commutes supply every lift, and InjectiveResolution.descHomotopy compares any two lifts of the same module map. Apply the proved total homotopy construction, extend it by zero, and use DerivedCategory.Q_map_eq_of_homotopy. This proves equality of the actual localized maps without any augmentation quasi-isomorphism hypothesis.

proof.text: Compare each composite of opposite identity lifts with the identity using localized lift uniqueness. Functor.map_comp and Functor.map_id give the two inverse equations, which construct the required isomorphism. The same uniqueness compares an identity lift with the identity map and a chosen composite lift with the composite of two lifts, giving identity and composition coherence.

proof.text: The assumed exact forgetful functor sends the augmentation I.ι' to a quasi-isomorphism; preservation of injectives makes its image complex termwise injective. It remains bounded below, hence is K-injective by Mathlib CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective. The Grothendieck hypotheses supply K-injective resolutions in the ambient categories. Define c by RF(QUι') followed by rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso on UI. The identity rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_eq proves both unit invertibility and the normalization equation. Map the augmentation-preserving lift square with U and Q, then use the existing unbounded rightDerivedFunctor_map_Q_map_comp_objQIso_hom naturality theorem to obtain the column square.

proof.text: For invariants, expand the existing normalized resolutionComparison. The lift defines InjectiveResolution.Hom, whose ι'_comp_hom' gives the integer-indexed augmentation square. Apply Q and RF, use rightDerivedFunctor_map_Q_map_comp_objQIso_hom, and then the naturality of mapExtendIso. This is the first asserted identity. The second follows by composing with the localized total augmentation and applying the strict naturality of TotalAugmentation.map. No invertibility of the total augmentation is used.
